content: Drooling refers to the unintentional flow of saliva outside the mouth. Symptoms of Drooling Drooling typically occurs due to one or more of the following reasons: Difficulty retaining saliva within the oral cavity. Impairment in the swallowing mechanism. Excessive production of saliva. Individuals experiencing drooling may face an increased risk of aspiration, which involves the inhalation of saliva, food, or liquids into the lungs. This can be particularly harmful if the body’s protective reflexes, such as gagging or coughing, are compromised. In cases where drooling is caused by neurological issues, it can often be managed with medications that inhibit the action of acetylcholine, a chemical messenger in the nervous system. These medications are known as anticholinergic drugs. For severe cases, interventions such as botulinum toxin injections, radiation therapy targeting the salivary glands, or other specialized treatments may be employed to reduce drooling. Causes of Drooling In infants and toddlers, some degree of drooling is normal and is not typically indicative of an underlying disease or disorder. It is often associated with teething. However, drooling in young children may worsen during upper respiratory infections or due to nasal allergies. Drooling accompanied by fever or difficulty swallowing may signal a more serious condition, such as: Infectious mononucleosis. Peritonsillar abscess. Retropharyngeal abscess. Streptococcal pharyngitis (strep throat). Tonsillitis. Sudden onset of drooling can also occur in cases of poisoning, particularly from pesticides, or as a reaction to venom from snake or insect bites. Other potential causes of drooling include: Certain medications. Neurological disorders affecting the nervous system. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care You should contact a healthcare provider if: The cause of the drooling has not been identified. There is concern about the risk of aspiration. A child presents with fever, difficulty breathing, or holds their head in an unusual position. Treatment Options For drooling related to teething, maintaining good oral hygiene is essential. Providing cold objects, such as popsicles or frozen bagels, may help alleviate symptoms. However, care must be taken to prevent choking when using these items. Where to Find Medical Care for Drooling Seek guidance from hospitals or medical facilities that specialize in treating drooling and its underlying causes. What to Expect (Outlook/Prognosis) A physician will perform a thorough physical examination and inquire about the patient’s symptoms. Questions may include: Is there a history of any other medical conditions? Has the individual experienced a bite or sting? Has there been any recent injury? What medications is the individual currently taking? Are there any accompanying symptoms, such as fever, sore throat, or facial droop? The diagnostic tests conducted will depend on the specific symptoms associated with the drooling.
